messages.content: Let’s settle the Chicago flights for the Friday-to-Monday arts weekend. It is still two of us, with the concert Saturday and the museum Sunday.

I found two practical nonstop choices each way. Friday’s midday flight leaves Denver at 12:15 p.m. and reaches O’Hare at 3:38 p.m.; the late flight leaves at 6:55 p.m. and reaches Midway at 10:12 p.m. Monday, there is an 8:20 a.m. departure from O’Hare or a 3:40 p.m. departure from Midway.
Give me the total airfare for two for each sensible pairing, not just the per-person fares.

For two travelers, midday Friday plus early Monday is $486. Midday Friday plus midafternoon Monday is $558. Late Friday plus early Monday is $398, and late Friday plus midafternoon Monday is $470. All four combinations are nonstop in both directions.
How much usable time do we really gain Friday by paying for the midday flight? Compare the airport transfers too, since the hotels we are considering are in River North.

The midday arrival at O’Hare should put you at a River North hotel around 4:45 to 5:15 p.m., allowing for deplaning, luggage, and a typical 45-to-70-minute drive. The late Midway arrival would likely put you there around 11:00 to 11:30 p.m.; Midway is usually a shorter 30-to-45-minute transfer at that hour. The extra $88 for two buys roughly six hours in Chicago and makes Friday evening usable rather than simply a travel night.
That seems worth it. Now compare the Monday choices. Checkout will probably be at noon, and I do not want the museum moved from Sunday.

The 8:20 a.m. O’Hare flight requires leaving River North around 5:30 a.m., so Monday contributes no downtown time. The 3:40 p.m. Midway flight lets you check out at noon, leave bags with the hotel, have lunch nearby, retrieve them around 1:00 p.m., and depart by about 1:20. It adds $72 total and gives you an unhurried morning plus lunch.
Would 1:20 be enough margin for Midway on a Monday? We will each have a carry-on, no checked luggage.

Yes. With a typical 30-to-45-minute ride, you would reach Midway around 1:50 to 2:05 p.m., leaving about 95 minutes before departure. To protect against traffic, I would finish lunch by 12:50 and have the hotel bring the bags out while one of you requests the car.
So the midday outbound and afternoon return are $558 for both, correct? What are the actual flight times and airlines?

Correct. United operates Friday’s nonstop from Denver at 12:15 p.m., arriving O’Hare at 3:38 p.m. Southwest operates Monday’s nonstop from Midway at 3:40 p.m., arriving Denver at 5:22 p.m. The combined airfare is $558 for two travelers, including Southwest’s standard carry-on allowance; United’s fare also permits one carry-on each.
Select those. For my seat, request a window. If the Monday seat map is not available until check-in, keep the flight and try for the window then rather than changing the itinerary.

The Friday United seat map currently has a standard window available for you, with an adjacent seat available for your spouse. Southwest does not assign seats on this fare at booking, so I have noted the window request for the earliest available check-in step without changing the selected flight.
Good. Summarize the schedule, transfers, and Monday bag plan before I confirm payment.

Selected for two adults, pending payment: Friday United nonstop from Denver at 12:15 p.m., arriving O’Hare at 3:38 p.m.; Monday Southwest nonstop from Midway at 3:40 p.m., arriving Denver at 5:22 p.m. Total airfare is $558. Allow 45 to 70 minutes from O’Hare to River North, putting you at the hotel around 4:45 to 5:15 Friday. On Monday, check out at noon, store both carry-ons with the hotel, have lunch nearby, retrieve the bags by 1:00 p.m., and leave for Midway around 1:20. Your Friday window seat can be selected now; the Monday window request must be handled when check-in opens. The Saturday concert and Sunday museum plan remain unchanged. Nothing has been charged yet.
